organization: Breathe California of the Bay Area, Golden Gate, and Central Coast
eyebrow: Exploratory whole-gift cost · partial clinical health
program: EIN 94-1156307; cessation, child/adult asthma and prescription CPAP access

nutshell.headline: A broad lung-health gift cannot inherit the price of one cessation course.
nutshell.body: The expanded clinical subset gives $5,739,210 per 10 Bay QALYs, retaining the full $100,000 gift. This is a conditional partial-health calculation—not complete whole-organization expected value, a guaranteed lower bound or a verified funding offer.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Additional supported quitting, asthma home visits and safe prescription CPAP access can improve health beyond existing care.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Marginal allocations, actual episodes, alternatives and geography are priors. CPAP quality-of-life results differ by instrument and include a negative EQ-5D bound; substantial portfolio benefits remain unquantified.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: No verified cash-created cohort or complete resource budget. Whole-organization expected QALYs remain unresolved, not zero.

steps.title: Adult cessation (15%)
steps.detail: Blended offered-course prior; not several independent people across delivery formats. Allocation is a marginal analyst prior, not audited spending.

steps.title: All-age asthma (25%)
steps.detail: Child home-visit health plus adult home-visit subset; workshops are not assigned the full home-visit effect. Allocation is a marginal analyst prior, not audited spending.

steps.title: Prescription CPAP (25%)
steps.detail: Safe donated equipment, consumables and external clinical calibration; replacements are not new people. Allocation is a marginal analyst prior, not audited spending.

steps.title: Senior/COPD (10%)
steps.detail: Education, assessment and referral; health unresolved, not silently classified as overhead. Allocation is a marginal analyst prior, not audited spending.

steps.title: Clean-air/youth (10%)
steps.detail: Unresolved activity effects; no extra credit for remediation already counted in asthma. Allocation is a marginal analyst prior, not audited spending.

steps.title: TB/other education (5%)
steps.detail: No verified additional diagnostic/treatment-completion cohort. Allocation is a marginal analyst prior, not audited spending.

steps.title: Central enabling cost (10%)
steps.detail: Already retained once in the full gift. Allocation is a marginal analyst prior, not audited spending.

programSection.boundary: Quantified allocations total 65%; remaining 25% distinct activities have unresolved health and 10% central cost is retained. Whole gift stays priced. Eight CPAP-eligible counties include Monterey, San Benito and Santa Cruz, so they are not eight Bay counties. No pooling of separate Breathe affiliates.

model.headline: Whole $100,000 cost; expanded clinical subset, not full expected return
model.body: Cessation uses finite smoking/quit/dead trajectories with later quitting, relapse and mortality in both arms. Child/adult asthma use distinct age and service fractions. CPAP uses one integrated trial year, not device-life multiplication. CPAP/asthma symptom dimensions can overlap within people; no duplicate survival bonus or claim of a fully modeled joint utility state.

equation.label: Conditional Bay clinical-subset calculation
equation.expression: Whole-gift cessation and child-asthma health + additional CPAP episodes × integrated one-year effect × transfer + adult home-visit symptom health, each geography-adjusted; signed harms retained
equation.result: 0.17424000265609785 Bay QALYs; $5,739,210 per 10 Bay QALYs. Whole-organization expected QALYs: unresolved.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: No scenario weights assigned and no whole-organization expected-value estimate. CPAP negative EQ-5D trial-bound and adverse symptom scenarios can make total quantified health negative; no finite positive price then exists. Trial confidence intervals do not become charity intervals. Unresolved senior/COPD, youth/environmental, TB/other and workshop health is not zero and prevents treating the subset as a guaranteed lower bound.
model.fundingBoundary: Verified funding room remains unknown. DHCS-funded asthma delivery managed by The Center at Sierra Health Foundation, Medi-Cal supports, Kick It California and existing providers/donors are baseline. CPAP low inventory or a waitlist does not prove cash rather than suitable machines, prescriptions or calibration is binding. The $132,250 gross partial envelope includes nominal external inputs even when financing replaces another funder, but omits unresolved branches’ outside resources. Fees are financing transfers, not free resources. No invoice, accepted restricted tranche or full economic-cost estimate is claimed.

evidence.population: Lung Health Study middle-aged adults with airway obstruction
evidence.result: Supports quitting-health mechanism over 14.5 years; intervention more intensive than Ash Kickers.
evidence.transfer: Do not read arm mortality as conditional state hazard or local course efficacy; all state coefficients are priors.

evidence.design: Healthy Homes II randomized active-comparator trial
evidence.transfer: Child share only, separate one-year utility/transfer priors. Adult benefit now uses separate adult evidence rather than extrapolation from children.

evidence.result: No overall between-group primary asthma-control advantage.
evidence.transfer: Different intervention, but supports explicit null sensitivity.

evidence.design: Official giving/domain plus historical municipal agreement
evidence.result: Legal identity distinguished from similarly named affiliates.
evidence.transfer: 18-county scope does not verify current SF marginal cohort or funding room.

evidence.design: PREDICT randomized trial and one-year economic evaluation
evidence.population: 278 adults age65+ with symptomatic obstructive sleep apnea; CPAP plus supportive care versus supportive care
evidence.transfer: Instrument dependence and signed bounds retained. Integrated ITT year includes adherence, survival and comparator access. No later device-life, cardiovascular or accident credit.

evidence.population: Established cardiovascular disease and minimally sleepy obstructive sleep apnea
evidence.transfer: Different population; supports withholding automatic survival/stroke-prevention credit, not a claim all CPAP symptom benefits are zero.

evidence.population: 366 low-income adults with uncontrolled asthma; about4.9 visits over one year
evidence.result: 2.02 additional symptom-free days/fortnight; no between-group urgent-care improvement.
evidence.transfer: Endpoint days are converted using explicit0.5 transfer,0.1 utility gap and at most one year. Lower-intensity workshops do not inherit home-visit effects.

evidence.design: Official Sleep Safe eligibility and delivery descriptions
evidence.population: Prescription holders in Alameda, Contra Costa, Monterey, San Benito, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara and Santa Cruz
evidence.result: Donated machines cleaned, consumables replaced; external prescription/calibration required; inventory/waiting limitations described.
evidence.transfer: Eight service counties are not all Bay counties. Safe additional completed episodes, actual fees and marginal stock/cash capacity are unmeasured.

reservations: Marginal allocations and unit costs are unverified.
Mortality recovery is a cohort-calendar proxy, not exact individual smoking history.
Public and alternative access can erase marginal health.
SF/Bay future health shares are priors.
Gross associated resource envelope is partial; unquantified branches' outside inputs are unmeasured.
Secondary financial extract is context only; current primary filing unavailable.
CPAP adds one-year health, not lifetime benefit per machine.
Signed CPAP instrument uncertainty materially changes the total.
Remaining25% distinct activities are not merely overhead and not assumed zero benefit.
excludedBenefits: Adult workshop-only, camp and caregiver benefits
CPAP cardiovascular mortality, accidents or post-first-year health
Cessation lifetime tail beyond finite model or duplicate disease rewards
Asthma mortality and health beyond one year
Full joint patient utility-state effects and complete outside-resource costs
